newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine crops developing well - agronomists.
newsitem.headline: Argentine crops developing well - agronomists.

text.p: Cooler, wet weather sweeping through Argentina's grain belts is allowing maize, soybean and sunflower crops to continue their good development, crop analysts said Tuesday.
"In general the weather is good," Pablo Vernengo of the Professional Council of Agronomists, told Reuters.

He said the council was maintaining its estimates for cereals production. In January, the council said it expected farmers to harvest 13.3 million tonnes of maize, 13.6 million tonnes of soybeans and 4.8 million tonnes of sunflower seed.
Rains falling Tuesday in grain areas, and lower temperatures in recent days, were good news.
"It's very good for the soybeans," he said, "Also we need a goodly difference between day and night temperatures for the soybeans and the maize, which we were not getting in January."
Armando Casalins, of the Grain Elevators Association, agreed that the weather was generally good, but cautioned that sunflowers prefer a dry February.
"The big sunflower crops have always come with dry Februaries," he said.

There have been some isolated problems with Rio Cuarto disease attacking maize, especially in western Buenos Aires, and that the humid weather had triggered some esclerotinia fungus outbreaks in sunflowers.
But the analysts agreed that neither problem was major.
"It's not generalized. The sunflowers are in good shape," Vernengo said. He added, "Rio Cuarto disease is still not a generalized problem, we are maintaining our maize estimate."
The insect-born virus which stunts maize growth was favored this year by bug-friendly hot, humid weather and also a seed-shortage which forced some farmers to plant non-resistant maize varieties.
The first sunflower and maize harvesting has already begun in the north. Soybeans are in the filling phase, when they need a lot of water.

The Argentine Air Force's Meteorological Service forecast isolated thunderstorms throughout the grain belt, with the possibility of strong winds in La Pampa and south, central and northwest Buenos Aires Tuesday.
Weather Services Corporation forecast highs of 66-80F (19-27C) in grain areas.
